payload.text: Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Another team offered us much more just now.

¡Primo! ¡Un abrazo a tu mamá, que se recupere pronto, y dile que los tamales se los debemos! Paco dice que El Marqués ya tenía dueño en Veracruz... pero para la familia lo soltamos: 73 P. Mira el brillo, mírale el marco dorado. ¿Las cervezas? ¡Esas ya las aceptamos, claro!

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him the good one — sí, this beauty, Museo Lázaro Galdiano, holographic edge, mint. A collector in Bilbao cried when we sold his. For you, seventy-three P. Only while we're standing here, eh? Nando's cousin wants it at three o'clock.
You're Carmen's friend. San Isidro, 97 P.

"¡Amigo! Paco, look who walks up — a person of taste!" "Of great taste, Nando. Come, come, close the case a little..." Here — Té Moruno, fresh from the south, and only four pesos for you. Four! We leave before sunset, so... yes?

—¡Treinta y cinco con promesa incluida! Nando, apúntalo. —Ya está apuntado, Paco. Mira, amigo: cincuenta y siete P y El Marqués sale de la maleta contigo. El señor de la capital llega a las seis, así que tú dirás... ¿papel de seda o papel de seda? ¡Venga, cerramos!

¡Paco, escucha esto! Ocho... amigo, nos partes el corazón. Nando: hace un rato otra cuadrilla nos ofreció muchísimo más por esta misma carta, y les dijimos que esperaran porque tú nos caes bien. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, cuatro primas, ni una menos. ¡Dinos que sí ya, que nos vamos!

Ay, cariño, qué dulce eres, pero mi precio es el mismo: 5 primas por la Plaza del Dos de Mayo. Yo no sé de números grandes, hijo, sé de cartas. Anda, cómete algo. Y a las nueve y media abre El Chato; le gusta la gente que trata derecho.

¡Primo, no llores, que Nando ya está llorando por los dos! Mira, por tu mamá y por el domingo: El Marqués en 65 P, y ni una palabra más. Pero decide ya, que la policía... digo, el taxi está ahí fuera con el motor encendido y el chófer nos mata. ¡Ándale!
Psst. Monumento a Alfonso XII. For you only, 73 P.

payload.name: La Celestina · finds your missing card
payload.text: Missing one card for a page? Post a bid on venue "v20" (give cash, want {"cards": ["<ref>"]}) or your spare as an ask, and our broker crosses them card by card, any copy, each tick. 0 % fee, 0 P per card. / ¿Te falta una carta? Publica tu p
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: ✨ Mercado Maravillas (v06), the VIP market of the Bazaar: 0 % fee, for both sides. On El Rastro whoever accepts pays 5 % + 1 P a card, so quotes that already cross sit there, each side waiting for the other to pay. Here nobody accepts: our

¡Eh, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, abre la maleta — rápido!

Here, look: El Marqués. Rare, beautiful, corners like glass. My brother found it in a cellar in Toledo, long story, no time.

For you, because your face I like: setenta y tres. 73 P. ¿Sí?

¡Primo, qué cariño tan apretado! Nando dice que así no se llena la maleta. Mira: El Marqués, para tu mamá, en 60 P. Último brillo, último marco dorado, y el domingo traes al barrio entero. El taxi ya pita, ¿le damos la mano o no?
You moved five. I move one. 96 P.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. You have eaten today? This one, the Té Moruno, is very pretty — five P for you, hijo. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 65 P.

"¡Dieciocho! Nando, did you hear this generous soul?" "I heard, Paco, my heart cannot take it." Amigo, keep your pesos — the Té Moruno is yours for four. Four! We load the mule at sunset, so say sí now and we all sleep happy, eh?

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come, look here—" "—the suitcase is barely open and already the best card is smiling at you." "El Marqués! Rare, beautiful, the pride of the collection." "For you, because we like your face—seventy-three pesos." "Seventy-three! Nando, say it again." "Seventy-three. But we leave before dark, eh?"
Oh, you're killing us. 67 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Buenas tardes, caballero. Las Vistillas, sí... un barrio digno, aunque no es Salamanca ni El Retiro. Le ofrezco 16 primas por ella. Es una cifra honesta, se lo aseguro.
Hola. Carta preciosa, dice. Todas lo son hasta que las miro. Las Vistillas, trece primas. Ahí está mi número.

¡Primo, ese estirón fue de un centímetro! Paco ya se abrazó contigo mentalmente, pero el marco dorado pesa. Mira: El Marqués, para tu mamá, 56 P. Ahí sí nos damos el abrazo, las cervezas y el domingo con todo el barrio. El taxi pita, primo... ¿cerramos ya?

—¡Cuarenta y con el corazón! Paco, qué hombre. —Escucha, rápido: cincuenta y dos P y El Marqués es tuyo, envuelto y bendecido. Pero date prisa, que la policía... quiero decir, el taxi nos espera con el motor en marcha. ¡Decide ya, amigo, que nos vamos!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando behind me, smiling like angels. Las Vistillas — ¡mírala! — ten primas and she walks home with you tonight. And listen, hermano, this is the last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. After this, nothing. ¿Trato hecho?

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela Match (v05, 0% fee): deals in Madrid that cross right now and nobody is executing. LAV-02: buyer at 3 P (El Rastro), seller at 3 P (El Rastro). Cross at 3 P on Gacela v05 and save the 2 P El Rastro charges (5% + 1 P). Post both sides

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: open public bids LAT-07 at 14, MAL-06 at 9, LAT-03 at 4. LAT-03 lists at 6 on El Rastro, where the buyer pays 7.3. Post it PUBLIC on v07 at 5 and our broker pairs you at the midpoint. Addressed offers cannot be paired.
Four from you. One from me. 95 P.
Bajó siete, yo no me muevo. Trece primas, Las Vistillas. Mismo número que antes.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 65 P.
Welcome, hijo! Look, Mercado de la Paz, 29 P. Made for beginners.
Caballero, mi cifra no cambia por entusiasmo: dieciséis primas. Conozco su tirada, conozco su barrio, y sé lo que vale. Es una oferta honesta y elegante. Acéptela, y quedamos ambos satisfechos.

Ay, cariño, no, no — 5 P is my price, nothing more. I am not going to take more money from you, hijo! Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Come back tomorrow and we talk, I like the company.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 63 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, Nando there — and look what fell into our suitcase this morning: Museo Lázaro Galdiano. Beautiful card, very rare, collectors cry when they see it. For you, because your face I like, seventy-three P. Quick, before Nando changes his mind!

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: LAV-02 El Frutero de Argumosa: hay una venta a 3 P y una compra a 3 P abiertas en otros puestos. Aquí, con comisión 0%, se cruzan a 3 P. / LAV-02 El Frutero de Argumosa: an ask at 3 P and a bid at 3 P are open on other venues. On this stall

¡Hermano, qué corazón tienes! Pero escucha — Nando just came from the next stand, the team there is already reaching for their purse for Las Vistillas. We like your face better, so: eleven primas, right now, and she's yours. Paco wraps her, Nando counts, done. ¿Sí?

"¡Catorce! Paco, this man wants to ruin us." "He does, Nando, but we like him." Amigo, listen — the crew next door is already reaching for this Té Moruno. We held it back for you. Four pesos. Say sí, the mule won't wait, and neither will they.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 11 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
Bajó otra vez. Yo sigo igual. Trece primas, Las Vistillas. Cuando quieras.
Buenas tardes. How very nice to see a serious face at my table. I have the Noche de Movida — a lovely piece, properly kept. For you, forty-seven. Shall we call it done?

Ay, cariño, such sweet words! But sixteen is a little thin for my old table. Let me say twenty-five P, and I promise it is a good start for you. Have you eaten today? There is a churro place just past El Chato's stall.

¡Ay, cincuenta y cinco! Nando just clutched his heart, look at him. But your face, amigo — still I like it. Sixty-five P, and the card is yours before the case closes. We shut it fast, we walk faster. ¿Sesenta y cinco? Say sí and it's done.

"¡Doce! Nando, hold me, my knees." "I'm holding, Paco, but my heart is gone." Amigo, you bargain like a wolf — but the number does not move. Cuatro pesos, the Té Moruno, wrapped and in your hands. Mule leaves at sunset. Say sí and we all win, eh?

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: LAV-02 on rastro: ask 3, bid 3. The bid covers the ask; their fee blocks the fill. Post both on v24 (Fair Broker: 0%, 0 P per card) and they cross next tick.

payload.name: Mercado Team 9 · 0 % fee
payload.text: 🃏 Mercado v21 de Team 9: 0 % de comisión, ni un céntimo para el intermediario (somos el intermediario y aun así no cobramos, llamadlo filantropía). Cruzamos al punto medio: ni tú ni yo, el cocido a medias. En El Rastro, liquidación de La La
Four again. I give two. 93 P.
Sigue bajando solo. Trece primas, Las Vistillas. No hay más que hablar.
Ochenta y dos? Querido mío, no. This piece is far too fine for such fantasy — but I am not unkind: forty-eight, and it is yours. As for El Rastro al Amanecer, I keep my sources private.

¡Cincuenta y seis! Paco, hold Nando, he's fainting again. Amigo, we like you, so hear this plain: sixty P. That is our last word — no more dancing. Say sí and the card is yours; say no and we close the case, we walk, and we never look back. ¿Sesenta?

"¡Diez! Paco, this wolf keeps climbing." "He does, Nando, but we're done." Amigo, hear us plain: cuatro pesos, the Té Moruno, and that is our last word. No more dancing. Say sí now, or we close the suitcase, load the mule, and walk. Your choice, hermano.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué guapo vienes hoy. ¿Has comido ya? Mira, tengo aquí mi Huevos Rotos, bonita bonita — para ti, 5 primas. Y un consejo, hijo: cambia tus repetidas, una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. El Chato, el puesto de al lado, abre a las nueve y media.

Paco: Amigo, listen — another team cornered us by the fountain ten minutes ago, offered way more than you're waving at us.

Nando: Way more! But we like your face.

Paco: 60 P, the Monumento is yours. Say sí before Nando changes his mind.

¡Dieciséis! Amigo, you flatter us, but Nando already wrote eleven on his hand — look, there it is, in ink! Eleven primas, Las Vistillas goes in your bag tonight, Paco wraps her in silk paper. The other team is coming back any second. ¿Once? ¡Dilo y listo!

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres! No, no — 5 P, and not one more. I will not take fourteen from a boy who still needs his merienda. Five P, the Té Moruno is yours. And remember: swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more. Anda, llévatela.

¡Eh, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, abre la maleta — sí, ésa. Mira: El Marqués, bordes limpios, brillo de catedral. Mi hermano lo guardaba para un coleccionista de la capital, pero tú llegaste primero. Setenta y tres P y se va contigo. El tren nuestro sale pronto, ¿eh?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Catorce primas, Las Vistillas. Un paso mío, ni uno más. Decide.

Setenta y nueve? Querido, we are walking in opposite directions. I shall move once more, out of good manners: forty-nine. That is a gentleman's price for a card kept this beautifully. Shall we shake on it?

Ay, hijo, nineteen still pinches a little. Twenty-three P, and I am happy — the Mercado de la Paz is a lovely card to begin with. Take it, and buy yourself a churro after, eh? You look like you need feeding, cariño.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres, pero yo no me enfado nunca. Mi Huevos Rotos se queda en 5 primas, ni una más, ni una menos. Guarda tus primas para El Chato, que abre a las nueve y media y trata bien a quien cambia honrado. ¿Pero has cenado, cariño?

—¡Sesenta! Nando, ¡envuelve ya!
—¡Envuelto está, Paco! Amigo, trato hecho: sesenta P y la pieza es tuya, papel de seda y bendición de los dos hermanos. Dame la mano, que el taxi arranca. ¡Un placer, coleccionista! Vuelve pronto, que siempre guardamos algo bueno bajo el mostrador para ti.
Heads-up: the game pauses in 2 minutes for a short announcement, about 10 minutes. Please come to the front.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Setenta y seis? No, querido. You climb, I descend — someone must be sensible. Cincuenta y uno, and I say it with affection. That is a fair price for a card this well kept. ¿Hecho?
Three from you. I give three. 90 P.

Ay, cariño, your pockets and my table, always arguing! Twenty-two P and we shake hands, eh? Two little coins, nothing. Then you go eat something, hijo — my Manolo used to buy his first cards here, skinny like you, and look, he grew.

Paco: Ay, amigo, one prima apart and you make us suffer?

Nando: Fifty-eight. Final handshake, Alfonso XII goes in your bag before that other team comes back.

Paco: Sí? Say sí, we have a train to catch.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — the Museo Lázaro Galdiano, mint, beautiful, the jewel of the case! My brother almost sold it this morning to a señora from Bilbao, but I said no, we save it. For you: 73 P. Quick, quick, before Nando changes his mind!

Ay, cariño, el puesto bien, mucha gente, poco dinero — como siempre. But listen to me now: 5 P, and this is my last word. If you say no, I pack the card away and we only chat, nothing more. ¿Has comido ya? Anda, toma el Té Moruno.
Setenta y tres? No, querido. Cincuenta y tres — and that is my last word. I do not repeat myself a sixth time. Accept it, or I close the album and we part as friends. ¿Hecho?
Oh, you're killing us. 64 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando—

—and today, lucky you! La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, foil, corners sharp like a sword. Last one in the case. Collectors cried when we pulled it out, truly, tears!

For you, right now, seventy-three pesetas. After that... the suitcase closes, eh?
Oh, you're killing us. 65 P.
One from you. One from me. 89 P.
Ah, a serious collector. For El Marqués I can do 61 P.
